condition_specific: cancer which may result from exposure to heat, radiation, or a known carcinogen
notes: NOTE: This benefit runs through the Kansas Police and Firemen's Retirement System (KP&F / KPERS pension track), not the workers' compensation system. The presumption applies to disability retirement claims, not WC claims. Cancer presumption limited to types that 'may, in general, result from exposure to heat, radiation, or a known carcinogen.' Same re-entry restriction applies. Part of KPERS pension system.

NOTE: This benefit runs through the Kansas Police and Firemen's Retirement System (KP&F / KPERS pension track), not the workers' compensation system. The presumption applies to disability retirement claims, not WC claims. Presumption applies after 5 years of credited service. If member ceased being a contributing member due to service-connected disability for 6+ months and then rejoined, the presumption for heart/lung/cancer does not apply again until re-contributing for 2 years or clear evidence of duty-connection. Presumption is part of pension/retirement system (KPERS), not standalone WC statute. Burden shifts to member or other party once employer presents contrary evidence.

condition_specific: Coronary or coronary artery disease; cerebrovascular injury (modified WC causation standard, not a presumption)
notes: This is not a rebuttable presumption -- it's a modified workers' compensation causation standard. To qualify, the claim must show (1) a specific identifiable work event, (2) that the cardiac or cerebrovascular event occurred within 24 hours of that event, and (3) that the event was the "prevailing factor" in causing it. The burden of proof never shifts to the employer. This standard was enacted in 2014 (L. 2014, ch. 25, § 1), applies to events on or after July 1, 2014, and was amended in 2024 (L. 2024, ch. 27, § 2). It exists separately from, and in addition to, the Kansas Police and Firemen's Retirement System (KP&F) pension presumption (KSA 74-4952) covered elsewhere in this dataset.

condition_specific: bloodborne pathogens (as defined by K.A.R. 28-71 regulations cross-referenced in KSA 65-128, including HIV, hepatitis B, hepatitis C, and other pathogens transmitted through blood or body fluids)
statute_citation: K.S.A. 74-4952 (as amended by L. 2019, ch. 50 / HB 2031)
notes: NOTE: This benefit runs through the Kansas Police and Firemen's Retirement System (KP&F / KPERS pension track), not the workers' compensation system. HB 2031 (L. 2019, ch. 50) added bloodborne pathogens to K.S.A. 74-4952 effective July 1, 2019. Pathogen definition references K.A.R. 28-71 bloodborne pathogen regulations. Requires 5+ years of credited KPERS service. Rebuttable by preponderance of evidence.
